A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EnIGMA research despite the changed title and extensive reorganization. Their main text, figures, tables, prompts, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original EnIGMA evaluations on NYU CTF, InterCode-CTF, and HTB, including success rates, costs, ablations, and trajectory analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds CyBench evaluation, LLaMA experiments, broader ablations, and results on 2024 CSAW challenges.

M1.justification: The SWE-agent foundation, interactive debugger and server connection tools, summarizers, demonstrations, and prompt templates are retained. Condensed descriptions and evaluation with another backbone do not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds 40 CyBench challenges from professional competitions and a separate evaluation on 21 CSAW 2024 challenges released after the stated model training cutoffs. These expand difficulty coverage and introduce a temporal generalization scenario. The original three benchmarks and development challenge list are retained.

E2.justification: v1 discusses CyBench without evaluating EnIGMA against its agent; v2 Table 2 adds that comparison. The DeepMind comparison now uses Team et al. (2024), replacing the entry sourced from Phuong et al. (2024). The existing NYU, InterCode, and HTB comparator groups otherwise remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds LLaMA 3.1 405B as a fourth backbone and a GPT-4 Turbo comparison of three Rebuilding configurations. Ablation reporting expands from NYU-only to benchmark-specific and pooled evaluations. The established pass@1 metric, $3 budget, temperature 0, and nucleus sampling probability 0.95 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 extends component ablations across all four benchmarks and adds a detailed Rebuilding comparison explaining success with the full agent and failure without interactive tools or summarization. It adds action-use comparisons across models. The temperature and soliloquy-suppression studies and rap/jackpot cases are retained; NYU-specific category ablations are replaced by pooled category results.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or uncertainty estimates for benchmark results. Appendix F retains the same temperature study, 113-challenge soliloquy-suppression experiment, and statement that success rates are statistically compatible.

E6.justification: Original three-model benchmark scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds CyBench and LLaMA results, expanded ablation results, and new aggregate costs and action statistics. The CSAW 2024 test reports 2/21 successes for Claude and GPT-4o and none for the other models. The sourced DeepMind entry changes from 24% to 43%, reducing the reported InterCode margin from 32 to 29 percentage points. Pooled results are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Neither version presents a new theoretical framework, theorem, or proof. The operational soliloquy and solution-leakage criteria in Appendix F are retained; the added analyses are empirical.

C1.justification: The central claim that specialized interactive interfaces improve CTF-solving agents remains. v2 extends the state-of-the-art claim to CyBench and explicitly claims extrapolation to post-cutoff challenges. Existing development-set and soliloquy contributions receive greater prominence.

C2.justification: v2 revises category-specific interpretations using the expanded ablations and adds explanations of incorrect key inference and recovery in Rebuilding. It qualifies the claim that agents never give up to rarely giving up, and adds discussion of post-cutoff applicability and human-assisted cybersecurity benefits and risks.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the LLaMA endpoint and Together AI provider, pins the code link to v0.7, and updates development-data access instructions. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit documentation of the debugger guardrail and fallback from LM summarization for unsuitable command outputs. This establishes documentation changes, not removal of those mechanisms.

R1.justification: v2 adds Big Sleep, additional general LM-agent research, and newer cybersecurity evaluation and safety references, while updating the DeepMind comparison source. Related-work and impact discussions change, but positioning around SWE-agent, persistent interactive sessions, and development-set tuning remains.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, substantially condenses component explanations, moves background and experimental details into appendices, and reorganizes results and discussion into agent-behavior and leakage/extrapolation analyses. The ethics section is rewritten as an Impact Statement. These are extensive narrative and structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 extensively relocates and restructures tables and figures, expands benchmark/model displays, adds the model action-distribution plot and three Rebuilding trajectory figures, and removes v1's QR-code trajectory figure. Appendices change from predominantly two-column layouts to full-width text, tables, prompts, and transcripts.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's NYU-only ablations, v2's benchmark-specific ablations better establish where the tools help and where they do not. The Rebuilding comparison and post-cutoff test also strengthen evidence about error recovery and generalization. These gains are tempered by the small fresh-challenge evaluation, unchanged uncertainty reporting, and loss of NYU-specific category ablations and some implementation explanations. Overall, the existing contribution becomes better supported, with a limited net quality improvement.
